title: Microsoft Purview: Purview SDK built into Microsoft Agent Framework for custom agents
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the applicable billing meter undocumented even though Microsoft's billing table covers classification and protection of custom AI interactions. The prerequisite DLP policy command also omits its mandatory policy name; the collection-policy automation needs a public-preview qualification.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to embed the Purview SDK in the Agent Framework SDK.
claims.quote: Purview SDK embedded in Agent Framework SDK enables developers to seamlessly integrate enterprise-grade security, compliance, and governance into the AI agents they build.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Developers can attach middleware that intercepts prompts and responses and checks them against Purview policies.
claims.quote: you can add Microsoft Purview policy middleware to intercept prompts and responses to determine if they meet the policies set up in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Learn documents Python and .NET versions of the integration.
claims.quote:
Python: Run `pip install agent-framework`.
.NET: Install from NuGet.

claims.claim: The integration supports inline blocking of sensitive content using DLP policies.
claims.quote: Inline blocking of sensitive content based on Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.

claims.claim: Purview logs AI interactions for Audit, Communication Compliance, Insider Risk Management, eDiscovery and Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: Log AI interactions in Purview for Audit, Communication Compliance, Insider Risk Management, eDiscovery, and Data Lifecycle Management.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents no tenant-wide setting to attach or require Purview middleware across custom Agent Framework agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Agent Framework middleware tenant admin setting enforce enable integration. Opened the Agent Framework Purview integration page, ai-entra-registered, developer/configurepurview and developer/use-the-api; none documents a tenant-wide middleware-enforcement switch.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Managing SDK-integrated, Entra-registered AI app interactions requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Managing these AI interactions with Microsoft Purview requires you to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: An Azure subscription with Microsoft Purview configured is a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Microsoft Azure subscription with Microsoft Purview configured.

claims.claim: The Python Agent Framework SDK installation command is pip install agent-framework.
claims.quote: Python: Run `pip install agent-framework`.

claims.claim: The .NET SDK is installed from NuGet.
claims.quote: .NET: Install from NuGet.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 subscription with an E5 license and pay-as-you-go billing setup.

claims.claim: Variable cost is appropriate because the integration requires metered pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: In the pay-as-you-go model, you're charged based on your usage of various pay-as-you-go features, based on the unit of consumption for the feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Attached middleware sends prompts and responses to Purview for evaluation.
claims.quote: Use Microsoft Purview APIs to send data into Microsoft Purview and support Purview policies associated with that data.

claims.claim: Members of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group can read captured prompts and responses in activity explorer.
claims.quote: Drill down to each activity to view details that include displaying the prompts and response when you're a member of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group.

claims.claim: Python policy evaluation fails closed when user ID, tenant or application location cannot be resolved.
claims.quote: Policy evaluation fails closed when the middleware can't resolve a user ID, tenant, or application location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Python ignore_exceptions setting bypasses enforcement for every error.
claims.quote: Set `ignore_exceptions` only when you deliberately prefer availability over enforcement; this setting bypasses enforcement for every error.

claims.claim: Python documentation advises deriving identity from a validated server-side token instead of caller-controlled message fields.
claims.quote: Derive identity from a validated server-side token rather than caller-controlled message fields.

claims.claim: Python agent middleware evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.
claims.quote: Evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.

claims.claim: Python agent middleware does not evaluate a model tool call before the tool executes.
claims.quote: Doesn't evaluate context-provider output or a model tool call before the tool runs.

claims.claim: Python chat middleware evaluates model tool calls before execution.
claims.quote: Evaluates context-provider output, replayed history, and model tool calls before execution. Tool results are evaluated on the next model call.

claims.claim: Both Python middleware types buffer streamed responses in full and prevent incremental content delivery.
claims.quote: Both middleware types buffer a streamed response in full and evaluate it before releasing any update. Streaming therefore doesn't deliver content incrementally while Purview middleware is attached.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Documented DLP support for Entra-registered AI apps blocks prompts based on sensitive information types and is app-scoped.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types. This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation and RestrictAccess UploadText/Block creates the described prompt-blocking rule.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true -GenerateIncidentReport @("siteadmin") -NotifyUser @("admin@contonso.onmicrosoft.com") -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row note
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Locations <app location> -EnforcementPlanes @("Application") is the prerequisite policy-creation call.
claims.quote:
The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the DLP policy. If the value contains spaces, enclose the value in quotation marks.
Position: 1
Mandatory: True
claims.fix: The printed call omits mandatory Name. Replace it in the first control's note with 'Create the policy first using Example 4 in the linked New-DlpComplianceRule reference.' Retain the following sentence about the portal not supporting this scenario. Example 4 includes Name and the Application enforcement plane.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Recommendations > Secure interactions from enterprise apps leads to the collection-policy recommendation.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic)
From DSPM for AI (classic) > Recommendations page, locate and select Secure interactions from enterprise apps

claims.claim: The printed Set-FeatureConfiguration call sets the collection policy's IsIngestionEnabled value to false.
claims.quote: Set-FeatureConfiguration "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -ScenarioConfig '{"Activities": ["UploadText", "DownloadText"], "EnforcementPlanes": ["Application"], "SensitiveTypeIds": ["All"], "IsIngestionEnabled": false}'
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: 'Set-FeatureConfiguration is in Public Preview, is not available in all organisations, and is subject to change.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/set-featureconfiguration to sources; that reference explicitly states this qualification.

claims.claim: New-FeatureConfiguration creates the collection policy.
claims.quote: New-FeatureConfiguration -FeatureScenario KnowYourData -Name "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -Mode Enable

claims.claim: Learn gives membership of the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role as an example of appropriate permissions for the portal workflow.
claims.quote: with an account that has appropriate permissions. For example, an account that's a member of the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role.
